post.description:
Analyse a product web page for legitimacy using the LangGraph analysis pipeline, paid from the account's credits.

Passes the page (client-supplied facts and/or HTML or cleaned text) through the graph, which extracts the
facts, runs the cheap skills in parallel, lets the triage decide on expensive ones, then synthesises a
reliability score, an explanation and the shopper verdict (in English). The analysis
price is taken from the balance up front and refunded when the page can't be analysed (score -1) or the
analysis fails. The same input analysed again within the hour is served from an in-memory cache, free of
charge. Nothing about the page or the result is stored; the ``report_token`` lets the caller report a wrong
result later (``POST /v1/reports``), sharing the page only then and only with their consent; the ``share_token``
lets them make the verdict public as a link (``POST /v1/shares``, without any account).

A request with only a ``url`` has the server fetch the page first (the web link checker). A page it can't check
that way is answered with a free 422: ``PAGE_UNAVAILABLE`` (couldn't be fetched), ``PAGE_BLOCKED`` (the shop
refuses automatic visitors, or answered with a bot check), ``PAGE_TOO_THIN`` (an empty shell that needs a
browser) or ``INVALID_URL``.

The caller is a wallet's session (``Authorization: Bearer <session token>``) or an API key (``Bearer ufk_…``).

:param body: The request body containing the page content and flags.
:param request: The FastAPI request (used to access the compiled graph).
:param address: The account (injected by require_account).
:return: Reliability score (0–100), explanation, verdict, the scorer's assessment, the balance left, a report
    token and a share token.
:raises InternalServerError: If the graph fails.
:raises GatewayTimeoutError: If the analysis takes longer than ``analysis_timeout_s``.
:raises asyncio.CancelledError: If the client hung up (after the refund).

Analyse a page like ``POST /v1/analyze``, streaming progress as server-sent events while skills finish.

Events: one ``step`` per finished node (``{"skill", "findings"}`` with the finding types, plus ``page_type``
once classified), then a final ``result`` (the ``POST /v1/analyze`` body, with all the evidence) or ``error``.
Charged like ``POST /v1/analyze``: free on a cache hit (the result comes at once), refunded on ``error``, a score
of -1, or when the client hangs up before the analysis finished. A finished result is cached first, so a client
that lost the connection gets it again for free by repeating the request. A URL-only request fetches the page
before the stream starts; a page that can't be checked is a free 422 (no stream), as for ``POST /v1/analyze``.

:param body: The request body containing the page content and flags.
:param request: The FastAPI request (used to access the compiled graph).
:param address: The account (injected by require_account).
:return: A ``text/event-stream`` response.

post.description:
Start a card (or other fiat) payment for a pack that tops up an API key, at the provider's hosted checkout.

The provider is the seller: it handles the buyer's details, invoice and sales tax/VAT; this service only learns
that the key was paid for. Credited the pack's value when the provider's webhook confirms the payment.

:param body: The key and the pack.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The checkout URL.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: While no fiat provider is configured, or it can't start a checkout.

get.description:
Whether a card checkout has been paid, and the pack's invite codes once: for the checkout page on the way back.

Needs the checkout's claim token (``X-Unfret-Claim``, from ``fiat-checkout``): the provider knows the checkout's
id, but never the token. The first response after payment returns the codes and wipes them. 404 for an unknown
checkout, a wrong or missing token, or one older than a month.

:param request: The incoming request.
:param response: The response (marked uncacheable: it changes once paid).
:param checkout_id: The checkout's id (from ``fiat-checkout``).
:param x_unfret_claim: The checkout's claim token.
:return: Paid or not, the pack size, and the invites the first time.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: While card payments are off.
:raises UnknownCheckoutError: For an unknown checkout or a wrong or missing claim token.

post.description:
Build the unsigned SOL or USDC transfer that buys a pack of credits; the buyer's wallet signs and sends it.

The pack costs its crypto price plus the VAT of the buyer's country (see ``vat`` in ``/v1/pricing``); the
transaction's memo names the stored quote. Credits arrive once the transfer is finalized (about 15–30 seconds):
what arrived, minus its VAT, credited to the paying wallet unless ``beneficiary`` or ``key_id`` says otherwise.
No sign-in needed: anyone may fund any wallet or API key.

:param body: Which pack, for whom, paid how, from where.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The transaction (base64), a Solana Pay link for phone wallets, and the price breakdown.

get.description:
Whether a purchase has been paid: for the checkout to show when the checks have arrived, and its invites once.

No sign-in: the quote's id (from ``purchase-tx`` or the QR code's ``X-Unfret-Quote`` header) is random, so only
whoever started the purchase knows it until the payment's memo puts it on chain, which shows as much already.
Says nothing about who pays or who gets the checks. Quotes are deleted a day after they expire (404 then). The
invite codes need the purchase's claim token too (``X-Unfret-Claim``), which never goes on chain; the first
response that carries it after payment returns them, and wipes them.

:param request: The incoming request.
:param response: The response (marked uncacheable: it changes once paid).
:param quote_id: The quote's id.
:param x_unfret_claim: The purchase's claim token (from ``purchase-tx`` or the QR code's ``X-Unfret-Claim``).
:return: Paid or not, and the pack size.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: Without a database.
:raises UnknownQuoteError: For an unknown, expired or malformed id.

The Solana Pay request for a pack as a QR code, for paying from a phone wallet.

The price (VAT included) and its breakdown are in the ``X-Unfret-Total-Usd`` and ``X-Unfret-Vat-Rate``
headers; the quote's id, to poll ``/v1/credits/quotes/{quote_id}`` with, in ``X-Unfret-Quote``, and the claim
token that collects the pack's invites with that poll in ``X-Unfret-Claim``; the Solana Pay link itself (to open
a wallet app on the same phone) in ``X-Unfret-Pay-Url``.

:param request: The incoming request.
:param checks: The pack size.
:param country: The buyer's country (ISO 3166 alpha-2), for VAT.
:param currency: ``SOL`` or ``USDC``.
:param beneficiary: The wallet to credit; without it the paying wallet is credited.
:param key_id: The API key to credit instead.
:return: An SVG image.

post.description:
Redeem an invite for the signed-in wallet or the API key: it adds ``invite_checks`` checks (``/v1/pricing``).

Only for an account that never had any checks: a wallet we've never credited (no purchase, refund or reward) or
an API key that was never topped up, and only once per account. Each code works once. Nothing about the code's
buyer is known here, and the account keeps only the fact that it redeemed one (not which). Refusals: 400
``INVALID_INVITE`` (not a code), 404 ``UNKNOWN_INVITE``, 409 ``INVITE_USED``, 403 ``INVITE_NOT_FOR_THIS_ACCOUNT``
(the account has had checks, or already redeemed an invite).

:param body: The code.
:param request: The incoming request.
:param account: The redeeming account (injected by require_account).
:return: What was added and the new balance.

post.description:
Report that a result is wrong. With ``consent``, this one check's page data is shared for review.

Send back the ``report_token`` from the result with the request and explanation exactly as they were, so the
report provably concerns a check this account got (for a URL-only check, the page is fetched again now).
Personal details are scrubbed before anything is stored. A page already in the queue counts the report as
confirmation; a page reviewed recently is ``already_known``. If the review shows the score was far off (30+
points outside the label's zone), the first reporter gets free checks. Limits: a few reports per account per
month, one per page.

:param body: The report.
:param request: The incoming request.
:param account: The reporting account (injected by require_account).
:return: The outcome.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: If reports are off (no session secret) or the queue is full.

post.description:
Make a result public as a link: ``/r/<id>``, for 90 days. Send it without Authorization; it names no account.

The token must match the url and the result exactly (a share can only show a verdict Unfret gave for that page)
and be under 7 days old. What is stored is what the preview shows: the verdict in the showcase's wording (no
score, never "scam" or "fraud"), the product's title and link, the shop and the day of the check; no quotes from
the page and nothing about who checked. A check that included checkout_content can't be shared. 20 shares per
visitor network per day.

:param body: The share token, the checked url and the result.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The id, the link and the delete code (shown this once).
:raises TooManyRequestsError: Over today's limit.
